Sellside Analysts' Memo · Avanza · built 3 November 2026

How the sell-side sees Avanza, and where its view is heading

What each broker on record thinks and how that has moved over twelve months, with the Investment Analyst's judgement on where the sell-side goes next.

  • Three kinds of content, each labelled. The brokers' own commentary, from 36 research reports produced between 11 May 2026 and 29 Oct 2026 (blue-edged cards). The Investment Analyst's reading of the sell-side, from its Layers 1 to 4 and three memos (purple-edged cards and the judgement boxes). This memo's summaries, tables and charts, which name their sources.
  • Breadth. 1473 passages from 8 research houses, plus consensus and investor views. Every house the research records on this stock is included, however briefly it appears.
  • Checks. Every quotation was matched word for word to its source by script, every summary sentence was checked against the passages, and every number survived the editing.
How current this is, and what was left out

The research reports run from 11 May 2026 to 29 October 2026, with broker views dated back to 2019. Amounts are in Swedish kronor (SEK) and financial years are calendar years. The latest dated rating or target action is DNB Carnegie's third-quarter review of 19 October 2026 (Buy, target cut to SEK 425); dated DNB Carnegie, Deutsche Bank and Jefferies notes of 22 and 23 October 2026 add peer and margin detail, mostly on Nordnet's results; reports of 22 and 29 October 2026 record Deutsche Bank (Buy, SEK 440) and Jefferies (Underperform, SEK 335) unchanged. The Investment Analyst's current work is dated 23 to 25 October 2026 (earlier memos 22 June and 22 September 2026), on FactSet revisions read 22 October 2026; the next results are the fourth-quarter report of 22 January 2027.

Three April-May 2026 passages (old research) restate DNB Carnegie views dated April 2025 to April 2026 and add nothing beyond later passages, so they are not used. Broker comments on Nordnet's own shares (DNB Carnegie's Nordnet target cut to SEK 380; Deutsche Bank's Nordnet Hold at SEK 360) and on Swedish banks' tax exposure are not presented as views on Avanza; views from before 2025 appear only as history.

The answer in brief

  1. Coverage is split: domestic and some global houses say Buy, three international houses stay negative.

    • Houses writing on Avanza: the research records DNB Carnegie, Deutsche Bank, Jefferies and Morgan Stanley in depth, with Bernstein and Berenberg in a few passages.
    • Houses commenting on something else: Nordea's passages are about Swedish interest rates and the economy, and ING's one passage is about European household savings; neither is a view on Avanza's shares.
    • FactSet breadth: the Investment Analyst counts 11 to 13 brokers in FactSet consensus (13 Oct 2026) and records six Buy or Overweight, three Hold, two Sell of eleven rated brokers (22 Sep 2026).
    • Buy share: FactSet's buy share was 50% on 22 Oct 2026, up 3 points over three months and 8 points over six; a report of 29 Oct 2026 records 47% on 28 Oct.
    • Most and least positive: among rated houses with commentary, Deutsche Bank (Buy, SEK 440) is most positive and Morgan Stanley (Underweight, SEK 200) least; FactSet also lists Nordea at SEK 465.
    Source: Research passages; Investment Analyst's September memo and Layer 1; FactSet revisions file.

  2. Headlines stayed upbeat until the third quarter; the last three months turned from momentum to miss.

    • Twelve months ago to April: every DNB Carnegie title from Avanza (Buy): Costs in check (17 Oct 2025) to Avanza (Buy): Strong start to 2026 – Q1 preview (13 Apr 2026) carries Buy, as do all its later titles.
    • Six months ago, Denmark entered the headlines: DNB Carnegie's first-quarter review of 22 Apr 2026 was titled Crossing the Øresund, the note that cut its target for Danish costs.
    • July momentum: DNB Carnegie's Strong income-driven Q2 beat (15 Jul 2026) and even Underperform-rated Jefferies' Good Flow and Trading Momentum (14 Jul 2026) are the period's most upbeat titles.
    • Last three months: DNB Carnegie's titles moved to Different trading pattern, fundamentals intact (6 Oct) and Soft income behind miss (19 Oct); Jefferies titled its 16 Oct note on a 2% Operating Profit Miss.
    • Pool-level tone: a report of 29 Jun 2026 called sell-side positioning cautious to bearish; a report of 16 Oct 2026, under the heading of constructive pre-earnings initiations, said Sell-side sentiment shifted significantly in the six months preceding the Q3 earnings release.
    Source: Brokers' note titles (ledger); research passages on consensus.

  3. Only DNB Carnegie moved its target often; two new houses initiated in opposite directions.

    • DNB Carnegie, Buy throughout 2026: target raised SEK 370 to 415 (13 Apr), cut to 408 for Danish costs (22 Apr), raised 420 to 430 after the second quarter (15 Jul), trimmed to 425 (19 Oct); no move from 408 to 420 is recorded (see conflicts).
    • Jefferies initiated negative: Underperform, SEK 335, on 8 Jul 2026, and kept both after the second and third quarters; reports of 22 and 29 Oct 2026 record the target as 11% below a SEK 376.30 reference price.
    • Deutsche Bank initiated positive: Buy, SEK 440, on 30 Sep 2026, and kept both after the third-quarter miss, publishing no revised estimates (recorded in a report of 29 Oct 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley static: its last dated move raised the target from SEK 193 to 200 in January 2025, at Underweight; reports to 17 Sep 2026 restate Underweight, SEK 200.
    • Consensus target drifted: SEK 393.5 on 18 Jun 2026, median SEK 420 on 18 Sep, SEK 420.96 on 16 Oct and SEK 412.58 on 28 Oct, after the third quarter.
    Source: Research passages; Investment Analyst's June and September memos.

  4. The framing moved from interest-rate risk to Denmark, then to income per customer after the miss.

    • Mid-2026, rates dominated: Morgan Stanley warned of severe interest income compression from rate cuts (recorded 11 Jun 2026) and argued deposit beta benefits have peaked (recorded 17 Sep 2026), and a report of 29 Jun 2026 tied cautious positioning to valuation and interest income compression.
    • From July, Denmark took over: Jefferies argued Avanza is taking a bigger chance on a smaller prize (8 Jul 2026); the Investment Analyst wrote The rate concern has been replaced by a growth-and-Denmark concern (22 Sep).
    • After the third quarter, monetisation: DNB Carnegie's Jonsson called the trading drop a temporary seasonal pattern rather than a structural loss of market relevance (recorded 16 Oct 2026); Jefferies cited income per customer down 6%.
    • The Investment Analyst's reading: The sell-side reads the same words two ways, with DNB Carnegie cyclical and Jefferies seeing structurally lower income per customer (Layer 1, 23 Oct 2026).
    Source: Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, DNB Carnegie passages; Investment Analyst's September memo and Layer 1.

  5. The houses that write on it agree third-quarter yields fell while assets grew; they disagree on which wins.

    • Yield pressure is agreed: Deutsche Bank and DNB Carnegie both put the third-quarter fund margin at 22.2 basis points and brokerage yield at 10.3 basis points, blaming the shift to index funds and to lower-priced Private Banking and Pro trading.
    • Index fund share: DNB Carnegie's 19 Oct 2026 report put index funds at 55.5% of fund capital; Deutsche Bank had cited above 53.8% on 30 Sep 2026.
    • Asset growth answer, Deutsche Bank: savings capital growing 16% a year to SEK 1.7 trillion by 2028, and gross brokerage yield stable around 11 basis points since 2018.
    • Asset growth answer, DNB Carnegie: Avanza took 32% of Swedish fund inflows in the third quarter, so margin compression is minor (19 Oct 2026).
    • Jefferies disagrees: Jefferies highlighted that profit growth would likely taper as competitive forces limit long-term pricing power (recorded in a report of 16 Oct 2026).
    Source: Deutsche Bank, DNB Carnegie, Jefferies passages.

  6. Denmark divides the houses on cost and payoff, though none models Danish revenue yet.

    • Cost estimates differ more than twofold: Avanza budgets SEK 120 to 150 million; Jefferies estimates SEK 340 to 380 million over three years (8 Jul 2026), more than Nordnet's German launch.
    • DNB Carnegie's reservation: DNB Carnegie said on 22 Apr 2026 that running dual IT platforms seems suboptimal over the long term and creates development risks; a report of 22 Oct 2026 records the same warning.
    • Deutsche Bank's optionality view: Deutsche Bank's Killian sees Denmark adding about 70% to the addressable market, upside not required for the core case (recorded in a report of 16 Oct 2026).
    • Berenberg's middle view: Berenberg called Denmark a relatively low-risk choice because of its similarity to Sweden but expects limited medium-term revenue (recorded in a report of 22 Oct 2026).
    • Cost guidance cut: DNB Carnegie noted on 19 Oct 2026 that Avanza cut its 2026 Danish spend to SEK 40 million, leaving the SEK 120 to 150 million total unchanged.
    Source: Jefferies, DNB Carnegie, Deutsche Bank, Berenberg passages; consensus passages.

    Danish costs: estimates differ more than twofold

    Danish cost estimates differ more than twofold: Avanza budgets SEK 120 to 150 million, while Jefferies estimates SEK 340 to 380 million over three years.

  7. Interest income is the swing factor: houses weigh rate sensitivity against deposit and lending growth differently.

    • Morgan Stanley bearish on rates: Morgan Stanley's analysts project severe net interest income contraction from rate cuts because deposit benefits have peaked (recorded in a report of 17 Sep 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie's internalisation case: ending the Sparkonto+ partner account lets Avanza earn a 50 basis point treasury spread instead of 5 basis points of commission (recorded 16 Oct 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie's rate sensitivity: a 25 basis point policy rate cut costs about 4% of pre-tax profit; three-month interbank rates (STIBOR) following the forward curve to 2.25% would add about 4% to 2027 earnings per share (19 Oct 2026).
    • Deutsche Bank's volume case: growing deposit and lending volumes offset lower rates, though a 100 basis point cut is a SEK 420 million interest income headwind.
    • Nordea's rate call, not an Avanza view: Nordea expects Riksbank hikes to 2.00% in November 2026 and 2.25% in February 2027.
    Source: Morgan Stanley, DNB Carnegie, Deutsche Bank, Nordea passages.

  8. Estimates rose strongly over twelve months, then stalled; most houses have not updated since the miss.

    • 2027 earnings per share revisions: FactSet consensus rose 13% over twelve months, 8% over six, 2% over three and 1% over one (read 22 Oct 2026); 2027 sales rose 11%, 5%, 1% and 1%.
    • Levels: FactSet median earnings per share on 13 Oct 2026 was SEK 19.40 (2026), 20.87 (2027) and 22.88 (2028), up from 19.39, 20.58 and 22.00 on 18 Sep.
    • Wide range for 2027: broker earnings per share runs from SEK 18.65 (Jefferies, recorded 16 Oct 2026) and SEK 19.29 (DNB Carnegie, 19 Oct) to SEK 22.85 (Deutsche Bank, 30 Sep).
    • Stale consensus: the Investment Analyst notes ten of thirteen houses are on pre-print numbers (two from July); a report of 29 Oct 2026 records the 2027 mean at SEK 21.13 on 28 Oct, unchanged since before the print.
    • Post-print cuts were small: DNB Carnegie trimmed 2026 to 2028 earnings per share by 0% to 1% on 19 Oct 2026, keeping a case for 17% upside to 2027 earnings per share if first-half activity per user returns.
    Source: FactSet revisions file; Investment Analyst's Layers 1, 3 and 4 and September memo; research passages.

    Consensus still predates the third-quarter miss

    Ten of thirteen houses are still on pre-print numbers, so the 13% twelve-month rise in 2027 earnings per share describes the period before the third-quarter miss.

  9. On valuation the bulls cite history, the bears cite peers and growth.

    • Deutsche Bank: Avanza at about 18 times 2027 earnings, about 30% below its ten-year average of 27.9 times and 13% above peers (30 Sep 2026).
    • DNB Carnegie: about 20 times 2027 earnings, a 15% discount to history that it calls unjustified, but Avanza should trade at a 10% to 20% discount to Nordnet (reports of 7 Aug and 16 Oct 2026).
    • Jefferies: a price-to-earnings-to-growth ratio of about 2 against Nordnet's 1.5 makes 21.2 times forward earnings demanding (recorded 16 Oct 2026).
    • Morgan Stanley: 22 times 2025 earnings was an unjustified 27% premium to European peers, with a bear-case scenario value of SEK 136 (recorded 11 Jun 2026).
    • Market level: the Investment Analyst puts the stock at 16.2 times current consensus (12th percentile of ten years) and the median target of SEK 430 at 19% above the SEK 360.1 price.
    Source: Deutsche Bank, DNB Carnegie, Jefferies, Morgan Stanley passages; Investment Analyst's memo.

  10. The market has rewarded Nordnet; investors focused on rates and Danish costs.

    • Second-quarter focus: a report of 7 Aug 2026 says expectations centered on potential margin pressure from Riksbank rate cuts and the cost trajectory of its newly announced Danish expansion.
    • Nordnet rewarded: the same report records Nordnet's 31.24% twelve-month share return against Avanza's relative return of (5.33)%, saying the market has heavily rewarded Nordnet's broader geographic business model.
    • Denmark doubts: a report of 11 Jun 2026 warns investor consensus may prove overly optimistic on Denmark.
    • Share price path: SEK 379.9 (18 Jun 2026), SEK 390.0 (22 Sep), SEK 376.30 (15 Oct), SEK 360.1 after the print, and SEK 351.6 on 2 Nov 2026.
    • Evidence gap: the Investment Analyst found no investor commentary in forums, social media or the Swedish financial press and records this as an evidence gap, and judges The narrative today is the one the Q3 print wrote.
    Source: Research passages on investors; Investment Analyst's memos and Layers 1, 3 and 4; stock facts.

  11. The Investment Analyst expects consensus cuts, not raises, over the next eighteen months.

    • Direction: the Investment Analyst judges Consensus for FY2026 and FY2027 is more likely to be cut, by 3% to 5% for 2027 over eighteen months (Layers 3 and 4, 24 Oct 2026).
    • Cycle: the Investment Analyst's memo states The estimate cycle has peaked. and calls 2027 the trough year of the earnings path.
    • A reversal from September: on 22 Sep 2026 the Investment Analyst had judged that upgrades over the next six to twelve months are probable.
    • Counter-case: the Investment Analyst records Deutsche Bank's case is that the asset engine overwhelms yield, and names a November Riksbank hold as a trigger to change its view.
    • Momentum signal: a report of 29 Oct 2026 records that the dashboard's sell-side earnings momentum rating moved from A to B, with revisions of 2% over one and three months.
    Source: Investment Analyst's Layers 3 and 4, memo and September memo; research passage of 29 Oct 2026.

Where the sell-side's view is heading

The Investment Analyst's judgement

The upgrade cycle has peaked: the Investment Analyst judges the twelve-month rise in estimates a lagging reading, and expects the next revisions to be cuts.

  • Twelve and six months: FY2027 earnings per share consensus rose 13% over twelve months and 8% over six, sales 11% and 5%; target price 6% and Buy share 8 points over six months.
  • Three months and one: momentum faded: earnings per share up only 2% over three months and 1% over one, the target price flat, though the Buy share rose 3 points to 50%.
  • What turned it: the Investment Analyst judges the upgrades came from cyclical trading and currency beats, not net interest income; the third-quarter print, a 2% operating profit miss, ended the cycle.
  • Most houses have not reacted: only three houses have published since 16 October and ten are on pre-print numbers, so the revision series describes the twelve months to the print.
  • Where consensus goes next: the Investment Analyst expects FY2027 consensus cut 3% to 5% over 18 months, the Buy share drifting toward 40% to 45% and the median target toward SEK 400 to 410.
  • Why: the Investment Analyst judges 2027 the earnings trough, with consensus holding the margin at 69.5% against the Investment Analyst's 68.2% as Danish costs arrive; the 22 January report is the first test.
  • What would prove it wrong: a return of H1 2026 trading velocity, or two of a second rate hike, rebuilding deposits and a low Swedish cost guide; the Investment Analyst puts this at about 10%.

What each broker says

Each research house in turn, ordered by how much the research records from it: its view in one line, then how it frames the case, its arguments, its worries and how its view changed. Quoted words are the research report's.

DNB CarnegieErmin Keric, Nicolas McBeath, Emil Jonsson, Liljeberg, Palin (earlier Jens Hallen)Buy, target SEK 425 (19 Oct 2026)

DNB Carnegie is the domestic bull: Buy in its titles since April 2025, it reads the third-quarter miss as cyclical but dislikes the separate Danish platform.

Stance and how it got there

  • From Hold to Buy: DNB Carnegie's titles mostly carry Hold through 2023 and 2024; its 4 Apr 2025 preview reads Long-term potential not priced in – BUY (Hold).
  • 2026 target path: DNB Carnegie raised its target from SEK 370 to 415 (13 Apr), cut it to 408 for Danish costs (22 Apr) and raised it from 420 to 430 (15 Jul).
  • Third-quarter review: on 19 Oct 2026 DNB Carnegie called the result incrementally negative, trimmed its target to SEK 425 from 430 and kept Buy.
  • Small estimate cuts: DNB Carnegie cut earnings per share to SEK 18.90 from 19.04 (2026), 19.29 from 19.34 (2027) and 20.79 from 20.93 (2028) on 19 Oct 2026.

How it frames the case

  • Asset gathering beats trading swings: DNB Carnegie's 19 Oct 2026 report says the long-term investment thesis remains firmly intact due to continuous user intake and resilient capital inflows.
  • Cheap against its own history: DNB Carnegie's McBeath put Avanza at about 20 times 2027 earnings, 15% below its historical average, a discount he called unjustified (recorded 16 Oct 2026).
  • But below Nordnet: DNB Carnegie argued Avanza should trade at a 10% to 20% discount to Nordnet because of higher cost inflation, and called the then 20% discount compelling (recorded 7 Aug 2026).

Main arguments

  • Deposit internalisation: DNB Carnegie's Keric said Avanza earns only 5 basis points of commission on Sparkonto+ but generates a 50 basis point treasury spread on its own accounts (recorded 16 Oct 2026).
  • Sigma discretionary service: DNB Carnegie said on 4 Sep 2026 that Sigma's fees sit above the 22 basis point fund margin, making it margin accretive, though it builds gradually.
  • Conditional upside: DNB Carnegie sees 17% upside to 2027 earnings per share if first-half trading per user returns, plus about 4% if short rates follow the forward curve to 2.25% (19 Oct 2026).
  • Share of inflows: DNB Carnegie said Avanza took 32% of Swedish fund inflows in the third quarter, so margin compression is minor (19 Oct 2026).

What worries it

  • Dual technology platforms: DNB Carnegie said on 22 Apr 2026 that running dual IT platforms seems suboptimal over the long term and creates development risks; a report of 22 Oct 2026 records the same warning.
  • Danish brand: DNB Carnegie warned on 19 Oct 2026 that Avanza will struggle to replicate its brand because Nordnet already holds a dominant position in Denmark.
  • Rate sensitivity: DNB Carnegie estimates a 25 basis point rate cut costs about 4% of pre-tax profit, and notes deposit betas already reached 80% (reports of 16 and 19 Oct 2026).
  • Costs and competition: DNB Carnegie's Keric said Avanza's elevated cost inflation remains a long-term risk (recorded 7 Aug 2026), and on 19 Oct flagged heightened competition in Private Banking remains a key concern.

How its view changed

  • Twelve months: DNB Carnegie's target rose from SEK 370 before 13 Apr 2026 to a peak of SEK 430 in July 2026, then eased to SEK 425; the rating stayed Buy.
  • Six months: Denmark became a standing reservation from the 22 Apr 2026 review, which cut the target for Danish costs; reports from 29 Jun 2026 record a 3% trim to 2026 to 2028 earnings per share for the same costs, without a date.
  • Three months: DNB Carnegie's titles went from Strong income-driven Q2 beat (15 Jul) to Soft income behind miss (19 Oct), but it kept Buy, treating the miss as sentiment.

Deutsche BankMiriam Killian, Goy (Pulvermacher and Sun also named)Buy, target SEK 440 (initiated 30 Sep 2026; kept after the third quarter, recorded 22 and 29 Oct 2026)

Deutsche Bank is the most bullish house with recorded commentary: Buy, SEK 440, since 30 Sep 2026, betting that savings growth overwhelms falling yields despite a third-quarter miss.

Stance and how it got there

  • Initiation: Deutsche Bank's Killian initiated at Buy with a SEK 440 target on 30 Sep 2026, with 2026 to 2028 net profit estimates 9% above consensus.
  • Top of the range: Deutsche Bank's 2027 earnings per share of SEK 22.85 is the highest broker forecast, with 14% compound growth in earnings per share over 2025 to 2028.
  • After the third quarter: Deutsche Bank kept Buy and SEK 440, citing inflows as evidence that the asset-growth engine remained intact (recorded in a report of 22 Oct 2026).
  • No reset: a report of 29 Oct 2026 records that Deutsche Bank published no revised estimate table after entering the third-quarter results about 17% above consensus on net profit.

How it frames the case

  • Pure play: Deutsche Bank called Avanza the purest digital platform exposure in Europe (30 Sep 2026).
  • Domestic wallet share: Deutsche Bank argued Avanza's dominant domestic position, high net promoter scores, and massive untapped wallet share outweigh near-term competitive pricing concerns (30 Sep 2026).
  • Denmark as an option: Deutsche Bank argued temporary forecasting errors in brokerage margins or minor cost overruns in Denmark will have negligible impacts on Avanza's earnings path (30 Sep 2026).

Main arguments

  • Savings growth: Deutsche Bank forecasts savings capital growing 16% a year to SEK 1.7 trillion by 2028 (30 Sep 2026).
  • Brokerage yield resilient: Deutsche Bank's September 2026 analysis shows gross brokerage yield stable around 11 basis points since 2018.
  • Valuation and peer choice: Deutsche Bank put Avanza at about 18 times 2027 earnings, about 30% below its ten-year average, and rates Nordnet only Hold at SEK 360.

What worries it

  • Nordnet's superior economics: Deutsche Bank's comparison shows Nordnet at a 76% operating margin and about 42% return on equity in 2025, against Avanza's 62% and 39%.
  • Losing ground on activity: Deutsche Bank's tracker shows September trades down 10% at Avanza against 5% at Nordnet, and customer growth of 8% against 12%.
  • Capital and rates: Deutsche Bank says deposit growth cut the leverage ratio to 4.7%, limiting distributions, and that a 100 basis point rate cut is a SEK 420 million interest income headwind.

How its view changed

  • Before September: Deutsche Bank's April 2026 trackers showed trading down 16%; a report of 29 Jun 2026 records Hold ratings by its analysts (see conflicts).
  • Third quarter tested the model: Deutsche Bank expected SEK 524 million of net interest income against SEK 464 million actual, which a 22 Oct 2026 report calls a material miss against the broker’s principal earnings catalyst.
  • Last three months: Deutsche Bank held its view, but a report of 29 Oct 2026 says nobody chased Deutsche Bank's above-consensus numbers.

JefferiesRoberts, Li, Mills, Gris TrilloUnderperform, target SEK 335 (initiated 8 Jul 2026; kept 16 Oct 2026)

Jefferies initiated at Underperform, SEK 335, on 8 Jul 2026: it admires the franchise but sees Denmark as costly, the valuation as demanding, and the miss as structural.

Stance and how it got there

  • Initiation: Jefferies' Roberts initiated at Underperform, SEK 335, on 8 Jul 2026, citing Danish execution risk and a price-to-earnings-to-growth ratio of about 2 on 21.2 times forward earnings.
  • After the second quarter: Jefferies kept SEK 335 while raising 2026 earnings per share 8% to SEK 19.68 and 2027 by 11% to SEK 20.73 (recorded 7 Aug 2026).
  • After the third quarter: Jefferies kept Underperform, SEK 335, on 16 Oct 2026; reports of 22 and 29 Oct record the target as 11% below a SEK 376.30 reference price.

How it frames the case

  • Good business, wrong price: Jefferies wrote on 8 Jul 2026 that Avanza's business is highly admirable due to its prominent domestic position and young customer base.
  • Bigger bet, smaller prize: Jefferies argued on 8 Jul 2026 that Avanza is taking a bigger chance on a smaller prize in Denmark than Nordnet in Germany.
  • Prefers Nordnet: Jefferies forecasts about 11% compound growth in earnings per share through 2028 for Nordnet against 8% for Avanza (recorded 22 Oct 2026).

Main arguments

  • Danish cost: Jefferies estimates the Danish launch at SEK 340 to 380 million over three years, against Avanza's SEK 120 to 150 million budget and Nordnet's SEK 200 to 230 million for Germany.
  • Income per customer: Jefferies said on 16 Oct 2026 that annualised income per customer fell 6% to SEK 2,170, with brokerage 5% below consensus as Pro traders paid lower rates.
  • Some offsets: Jefferies notes Avanza is better positioned during rate-cut cycles than Nordnet, and called the Sigma launch, at SEK 710 million of assets, a success (16 Oct 2026).

What worries it

  • Competition: Jefferies argues Interactive Brokers' Swedish investment savings accounts will intensify pricing pressure on active traders (8 Jul 2026), with eToro and Lightyear also cited (recorded 24 Oct 2026).
  • New technology: Jefferies' Roberts warned open-source artificial intelligence coding tools could significantly lower barriers to entry for low-cost neobrokers (recorded 16 Oct 2026).
  • Scenario values, not targets: Jefferies' downside scenario, with 60% margins and zero earnings growth, gives SEK 260 (16 Jul 2026); its upside scenario, with 15% revenue growth and buybacks, gives SEK 435 (recorded 24 Oct 2026).
  • Capital: Jefferies expects no share buybacks because on-balance-sheet deposit growth absorbs capital (recorded 24 Oct 2026).

How its view changed

  • July warmth in titles: Jefferies' 14 Jul 2026 note was titled Good Flow and Trading Momentum, and its 16 Jul note raised earnings per share estimates, without moving the rating or target.
  • Third quarter hardened it: a report of 22 Oct 2026 says the miss reinforced their pre-existing concern about income per customer, pricing, Denmark and technology investment.
  • 2027 estimate: a report of 16 Oct 2026 records Jefferies at SEK 18.65 for 2027 earnings per share, below consensus; no dated cut from SEK 20.73 is recorded (see conflicts).

Morgan StanleyPanos Ellinas, Bruce Hamilton, Marina MassutiUnderweight, target SEK 200 (raised from SEK 193 in January 2025; restated in reports to 17 Sep 2026)

Morgan Stanley is the long-running bear: Underweight since mid-2022 with the street-low SEK 200 target, arguing interest income has peaked and the multiple is unjustified.

Stance and how it got there

  • Underweight since mid-2022: Morgan Stanley cut its target from SEK 202 to 193 on cloud costs (12 Nov 2024), then raised it to SEK 200 in January 2025 after a strong fourth quarter.
  • Restated in 2026: reports of 11 Jun and 17 Sep 2026 restate Underweight and a base-case SEK 200, which a report of 18 Aug 2026 says comes from a discounted cash flow; the SEK 136 bear case is a scenario value.
  • Disputed upgrade: two reports of 2026 say Morgan Stanley upgraded to Overweight in early 2025, which the dated record of Underweight on 21 Jan 2025 contradicts (see conflicts).

How it frames the case

  • Low-quality beats: Morgan Stanley has focused on the low quality of Avanza's beats, with interest income masking weak transactions (recorded 31 May 2026).
  • Peak deposit benefit: Morgan Stanley's analysts project severe interest income contraction from rate cuts because deposit beta benefits have peaked (recorded 17 Sep 2026).
  • Concentration: Ellinas argued in January 2025 that geographic concentration in Sweden severely limits its total customer growth prospects relative to pan-Nordic peers.

Main arguments

  • Weak earnings path: Morgan Stanley forecasts earnings growth of (4)% a year over 2024 to 2026, and about 10% a year over 2025 to 2027 (reports of 11 Jun and 18 Aug 2026).
  • Valuation: Morgan Stanley calls 22 times 2025 earnings an unjustified 27% premium to European peers and sees the highest de-rating risk among European digital wealth platforms; on 3 Sep 2026 it noted Avanza still trades at a premium to peer averages.
  • Slower growth than Nordnet: Morgan Stanley projects Nordnet's top line growing 10% a year against 3% for Avanza (recorded 11 Jun 2026).
  • A positive: Morgan Stanley expects Swedish recovery to drive 13% compound growth in transaction revenues (recorded 17 Sep 2026).

What worries it

  • Cloud costs: Morgan Stanley estimates the cloud migration costs SEK 300 million by 2030 and projects cost pressures dragging the operating margin to 61% by 2026; its bear case has margins at 56% (recorded 11 Jun 2026).
  • Deposit mix: Morgan Stanley highlights client cash shifting to higher-yielding savings accounts, and revised its model to 50% pass-through of rate cuts (recorded 18 Aug 2026).

How its view changed

  • No change in twelve months: the research records no Morgan Stanley rating or target change since January 2025, and no Morgan Stanley note title after 21 Jan 2025.
  • Last title recorded: Morgan Stanley's latest dated title is Avanza: Positive FY24 print, NII outlook likely better (21 Jan 2025), a softer tone than Avanza: Challenges on all fronts (31 Oct 2023).

BernsteinAleksander Peterc, Ian WhiteUnderperform, target SEK 272 (as of May 2025; restated in reports of June 2026)

Bernstein rates Avanza Underperform with a SEK 272 target (May 2025), arguing Swedish penetration caps growth and cloud migration adds cost.

Main arguments

  • Growth ceiling: Bernstein's Peterc observes that reaching 25% penetration of the Swedish adult population implies a natural ceiling on future domestic growth (May 2025).
  • Cloud migration: Bernstein's White estimates the migration adds about SEK 300 million of operating expenses through 2030, though Bernstein's 8 May 2025 report calls it essential for scalability.
  • Open question: Bernstein asks how Avanza will protect its digital architecture from hyperscaler pricing power (recorded in a report of 11 Jun 2026).

NordeaTorbjörn IsakssonNo rating recorded; target SEK 465 on pre-print numbers (Investment Analyst's FactSet list)

Nordea's passages comment on Swedish interest rates and the economy, not on Avanza's shares; the Investment Analyst's FactSet list separately records a Nordea target of SEK 465, and the Investment Analyst counts Nordea among the bulls.

Main arguments

  • Rate path, not an Avanza view: Nordea's Isaksson expects the Riksbank to hike to 2.00% in November 2026 and to 2.25% in February 2027 (recorded 24 Oct 2026), which a report of 16 Oct 2026 says Nordea calls the cycle's peak.
  • Economy: Nordea reports recovering Swedish household confidence and credit growth of SEK 15 billion a month (recorded 16 Oct 2026).
  • Link to Avanza unclear: a report of 24 Oct 2026 says the higher rates would benefit Avanza's deposit margins; the passage does not make clear whether that inference is Nordea's.
  • Highest recorded target: Nordea's SEK 465 target in FactSet is the highest recorded; no Nordea rating or research commentary on Avanza's shares is recorded, but the Investment Analyst's Layer 1 lists the bulls (Deutsche Bank, Nordea, Pareto), and Layers 3 and 4 cite Nordea's SEK 22.70 for 2027 earnings per share.

Where the brokers disagree

Was the third-quarter revenue miss cyclical or structural?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie (19 Oct 2026): the trading drop was seasonal sentiment, user intake and inflows were resilient, and 2027 earnings per share has 17% upside if first-half activity returns.
  • Deutsche Bank (report of 22 Oct 2026): kept Buy, regarding 21% savings-capital growth and SEK 23.1 billion of inflows as proof the asset engine is intact, without calling the effects permanent.

The more negative side

  • Jefferies (16 Oct 2026): income per customer fell 6% to SEK 2,170 and brokerage missed by 5% on cheaper Pro trading; a 22 Oct report says Jefferies' concern was reinforced.
  • Morgan Stanley (record to 17 Sep 2026): has long argued Avanza's beats are low quality, with interest income masking weak transactions.

Will rates and deposits help or hurt net interest income?

The more positive side

  • DNB Carnegie (recorded 16 Oct; 19 Oct 2026): Sparkonto+ internalisation earns 50 basis points instead of 5, and three-month interbank rates following the forward curve to 2.25% would add about 4% to 2027 earnings per share.
  • Deutsche Bank (30 Sep 2026): growing deposit and lending volumes offset lower rates; a report of 24 Oct 2026 records its view that net interest income could comfortably exceed consensus.
  • Jefferies (recorded 17 Sep 2026): Avanza is less dependent on interest income than Nordnet and better placed in rate cuts.

The more negative side

  • Morgan Stanley (recorded 17 Sep 2026): projects severe interest income contraction because deposit benefits have peaked.
  • DNB Carnegie's own caution (19 Oct 2026; recorded 16 Oct): a 25 basis point cut costs about 4% of pre-tax profit, and deposit betas of 80% leave no buffer.
  • Deutsche Bank's third quarter: net interest income of SEK 464 million against its SEK 524 million forecast (recorded 22 Oct 2026).

Is the Danish entry worth its cost and risk?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank (30 Sep 2026; recorded 16 Oct 2026): Denmark adds about 70% to the addressable market, offers twice Sweden's median wealth, and is optional for the core case.
  • DNB Carnegie (19 Oct 2026): the SEK 120 to 150 million budget is minor and bounded, and the cut in 2026 spend to SEK 40 million shows discipline.
  • Berenberg (recorded 22 Oct 2026): Denmark is relatively low-risk because it resembles Sweden.

The more negative side

  • Jefferies (8 Jul 2026 onwards): a bigger chance on a smaller prize, costing SEK 340 to 380 million over three years against Nordnet's SEK 200 to 230 million for Germany.
  • DNB Carnegie (22 Apr and 19 Oct 2026): dual technology platforms look suboptimal, and Nordnet's dominance makes Avanza's brand hard to replicate.
  • Berenberg (recorded 22 Oct 2026): expects limited medium-term revenue in a smaller, competitive market.

Is the valuation cheap or demanding?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank (30 Sep 2026): about 18 times 2027 earnings is about 30% below the ten-year average, so risks look priced in.
  • DNB Carnegie (16 and 19 Oct 2026): about 20 times 2027 earnings is a 15% discount to history, which it calls unjustified given a sticky, young customer base.

The more negative side

  • Jefferies (recorded 16 Oct 2026): a price-to-earnings-to-growth ratio of about 2 against Nordnet's 1.5 makes 21.2 times forward earnings demanding.
  • Morgan Stanley (recorded 11 Jun 2026): 22 times 2025 earnings is an unjustified 27% premium to European peers, with de-rating risk toward the ten-year average of 18 times.
  • DNB Carnegie's peer view (recorded 7 Aug 2026): Avanza should still trade 10% to 20% below Nordnet because of higher cost inflation.

Avanza or Nordnet: which platform is better placed?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank (recorded 22 Oct 2026): rates Avanza Buy at SEK 440 and Nordnet Hold at SEK 360, seeing more domestic white space and a lower valuation at Avanza.
  • DNB Carnegie (6 and 19 Oct 2026): Avanza has a stronger brand and Swedish share than Nordnet has in any single market, and trades at 17.2 times 2027 earnings against Nordnet's 20.3 times.

The more negative side

  • Jefferies (recorded 22 Oct 2026): prefers Nordnet, forecasting about 11% compound growth in earnings per share through 2028 against 8% for Avanza.
  • Morgan Stanley (recorded 11 Jun 2026): projects Nordnet's top line growing 10% a year against 3% for Avanza.
  • Deutsche Bank's own data (recorded 22 Oct 2026): Nordnet's 2025 operating margin of 76% and return on equity of 42% beat Avanza's 62% and 39%, and Nordnet grew customers faster.

Is fee and yield compression temporary or permanent?

The more positive side

  • Deutsche Bank (September 2026): gross brokerage yield has held around 11 basis points since 2018, so compression looks transient.
  • DNB Carnegie (19 Oct 2026): unchanged retail prices and a stable customer base make the third-quarter yield fall a seasonal mix issue.

The more negative side

  • Jefferies (8 Jul 2026; recorded 24 Oct 2026): Interactive Brokers, eToro and Lightyear could push operating margins toward 60%, and index-fund migration is a structural drag.
  • DNB Carnegie's caution (19 Oct 2026): index funds reached 55.5% of fund capital, and Private Banking competition is a key concern.
  • Morgan Stanley (recorded 11 Jun 2026): active-to-passive shifts dilute average fund fee margins over time.

Where the research reports conflict. Both versions are shown; this memo does not pick one.
  1. Morgan Stanley's rating in early 2025.
    • Underweight version: a report of 17 Sep 2026 lists Morgan Stanley January 21, 2025 Underweight / Underweight SEK 200 / SEK 200, and another says Underweight since mid-2022.
    • Overweight version: reports of 11 Jun and 25 Oct 2026 say Morgan Stanley temporarily upgraded Avanza to Overweight in early 2025.
    • Unsettled: no passage dates an upgrade or a return to Underweight, so the inputs do not show whether an Overweight rating existed.
  2. Deutsche Bank: Hold in June, initiation at Buy in September.
    • Hold version: a report of 29 Jun 2026 says Deutsche Bank analysts Olivia Pulvermacher and Mengxian Sun maintain Hold ratings tracking retail platform metrics monthly.
    • Initiation version: several reports say Deutsche Bank initiated coverage with Buy and SEK 440 on 30 Sep 2026, which implies no earlier rating.
    • Unsettled: a report of 22 Oct 2026 names Pulvermacher, Sun and Killian together; the inputs do not show whether the Hold applied to Avanza.
  3. DNB Carnegie's target between April and July 2026.
    • Dated record: DNB Carnegie cut its target from SEK 415 to 408 on 22 Apr 2026, then raised it from SEK 420 to 430 on 15 Jul 2026.
    • Other versions: a report of 31 May 2026 still gives SEK 415, and a report of 7 Aug 2026 describes the path as 408 straight to 430, though the same report elsewhere says from SEK 420.
    • Unsettled: no passage records when, or whether, DNB Carnegie moved from SEK 408 to 420.
    • Earlier path: a report of 11 Jun 2026 says DNB Carnegie lifted its target from SEK 360 to 380 through late 2025, yet its April 2026 raise starts from SEK 370.
  4. DNB Carnegie's rating between September 2024 and January 2025.
    • Buy titles: DNB Carnegie notes titled Avanza Bank (Buy, TP: SEK300.00) - Do not discount Sweden yet (25 Sep 2024) and Avanza Bank (Buy, TP: SEK360.00) (21 Jan 2025).
    • Hold titles: DNB Carnegie notes on 7 Oct 2024, 21 Oct 2024 and 22 Jan 2025 carry Avanza (Hold), and the 4 Apr 2025 title reads BUY (Hold), an upgrade.
    • Unsettled: the two title series disagree on the rating for four months; the inputs do not show which applied.
  5. Jefferies' 2027 earnings per share and the multiple behind its target.
    • August version: a report of 7 Aug 2026 says Jefferies raised 2027 earnings per share by 11% to SEK 20.73 and called 17.1 times 2027 earnings demanding.
    • October version: a report of 16 Oct 2026 gives Jefferies' 2027 earnings per share as SEK 18.65, about 21 times 2027 earnings, at the same SEK 335 target.
    • Range claim: a report of 24 Oct 2026 says broker 2027 forecasts start at DNB Carnegie's SEK 19.29, which is above Jefferies' SEK 18.65, and the Investment Analyst's Layers 3 and 4 say Jefferies' FactSet estimates date from July; no dated Jefferies cut is recorded.
  6. Jefferies on Avanza's customer acquisition cost.
    • Expensive version: a report says Jefferies put Avanza's acquisition cost at SEK 8,263, higher than Nordnet's SEK 6,169, implying unproven economics (8 Jul 2026).
    • Efficient version: another report reads the same SEK 8,263 as immense efficiency against AJ Bell and FinecoBank, and the same report cites Jefferies on virtually zero customer acquisition costs (16 Oct 2026).
    • Unsettled: the inputs do not show which reading is Jefferies' own.
  7. Which target is the street high, and how bullish is the pool?
    • Report version: a report of 17 Sep 2026 calls DNB Carnegie's SEK 430 the street-high target and Morgan Stanley's SEK 200 the street-low, and puts Refinitiv's mix at 17% Overweight, 50% Equal-weight, 33% Underweight.
    • FactSet version: the Investment Analyst's list has Nordea at SEK 465, Pareto at 450 and restricted Buys at 450 and 460, with a 50% buy share on 22 Oct 2026.
    • Unsettled: the two sources cover different broker sets and dates; the inputs do not reconcile them.
  8. DNB Carnegie's numbers around the third quarter.
    • Upside size: a report of 16 Oct 2026 gives DNB Carnegie's conditional 2027 upside as 15%, next to its 6 Oct preview, while reports of its 19 Oct review give 17% and a report of 29 Oct 2026 says now 17%; the inputs do not say whether it was raised.
    • Multiple at the target: a report of 22 Oct 2026 says the SEK 425 target values Avanza at about 18 times 2027 earnings, while the same report, describing the earlier SEK 430 target, says roughly 20 times.
